features: THE LIMIT THAT WASN'T THERE — No migration, no changes to the calculation engine: the database is not touched. It starts from a forum report and ends on a document for the owners' meeting. The administrator asked why the program stopped at 40 property units; the answer is that it did not stop at all, and looking for the reason uncovered a defect that made money disappear from a printout.

THE LIMIT THAT DID NOT EXIST. An administrator with 67 units stopped at 40 and asked why the limit was so tight. There was no limit: the millesimi page links units, it does not create them, and that building had 40 on file. The defect was the message, which read like a cap imposed by the program. It now states the cause and where to fix it, in all four languages. Next to the button you can see how many units are still to be linked, so the limit is understood before you hit it. The count was corrected too: it compared the number of rows with the number of units, so a freshly added empty row took up a slot without using up any unit.

SIX EUROS IN TEN VANISHING FROM THE PER-CHAPTER BREAKDOWN. The program prints the same breakdown in two documents, by table and by chapter. The first builds its rows from the instalments actually issued, the second recalculated them live: an owner detached from the unit after the instalments were issued appeared in the first and vanished from the second, with the columns still adding up among themselves and nothing flagging anything. On a € 1,000.00 breakdown with a detached owner worth € 600.00, the per-chapter document showed € 400.00. That amount now appears in an «Outside the breakdown» column. Also fixed in the same printout: the bare-ownership abbreviation the legend did not know, and the tracking of shares no party can receive.

WHO OWNS WHAT, FROM THE LIST OF UNITS. The property units list showed the block, the land registry details and the square metres, but not who owns or lives in the unit. There is now a «Parties» column with everyone's initials and, on click, a panel with name, role, share and address. An owner whose end date has already passed stays visible with a «until …» note, because the breakdown still charges them.

DETACHING A PARTY NOW SAYS WHAT IT ENTAILS. If the party already has instalments issued, the confirmation explains that those instalments stay charged to them in the payment plan while they disappear from the unit's record, and that the breakdown does not yet take competence dates into account.

WHAT THIS VERSION DOES NOT DO. A fix to the importer was written and withdrawn before release: re-importing a corrected file duplicates the ownership records, but the fix asked for a decision no screen allowed the administrator to make, and the import would have stopped halfway with no way out. The defect remains open and documented. Also out of scope: the breakdown reading competence dates, and the real change-of-ownership operation.
